I initially gave this episode a rating of two—I now wish I'd given it more thought. I also wish there were negative rating options. Watching it, I was amazed at how poor the whole thing was from start to finish. I adore the actors and the director... so what went wrong?? Last season episode 13 was pulled due to the way it handled the abortion issue. I think that this season the director managed to make something so grey-area that you can't immediately see if they are pro-choice or anti-abortion. It was only after I sat and thought about it that I realized they are very much anti-abortion— you get this most clearly in the end when the 'Mother' shoots the baby and kills it, to the dismay of the 'Father', who walks off in grief, leaving the mother unharmed. But you also see it in the way the actor character is treated— I hardly think that if someone has proved themselves enough of a threat in the past so as to have a restraining order against them that they would not immediately be ringing the police. Instead we have the guard almost sympathetically dealing with them (only to pay for it in the end). I don't mind someone having a strong view on something, even if it isn't something I agree with, but I do think it's a bit lame not to stand by that view, rather than trying to look like they're sitting somewhere in the middle. But, political issues aside, this episode was beyond poor. The music was retro and just plain didn't work. The acting (other than the actor) was poor. The effects were dreadful— it might have been better just to not show the monster at all rather than show the lame excuse for a monster they had. All this being said, I'm glad they have the Masters of Horror—I don't mind sitting through some really poor episodes to find the good ones. It's a bit like renting horror movies from the video store— every now and again you get a good one and it makes it all worth while. I do agree with the poster that said maybe the name needs to change from Masters— some of these people just plain don't deserve the title. (Let me stress though— even though I hated this episode, the director totally deserves the title. They are a master through and through)

I can give you four reasons to see this movie: 1. Four of the best filmmakers in the contemporary regional cinema. 2. Four good stories, related into a big scheme. 3. A surprisingly good cast. 4. A bitter reflection about the biggest trouble in this country (and many others). (POSSIBLE SPOILERS) Alex opens this movie with a good story in a comedic mood about the authority practicing the extortion against regular people and still expecting to be appreciated by its efforts. Then Tony gets more dramatic in the second piece with a story heir to the Italian neorealism with a "Peter and the wolf"-like anecdote. In the third story, the one that seems more independent from this series even in the context, Carlos tells us the story of a man being at the wrong place in the wrong moment. But after the recent lynching and the tradition in this awful matter, this story couldn't be more updated. And at the end, Fernando returns to the dark humor in the "grand finale" in which he puts together the most of the characters from the past sequences in one of the better comedy pieces ever filmed. Reprising the center scene from one of his previous films, Fernando gives the final lesson of the theme. And by the way, give us the scene that steals the movie with Anna making a brief striptease. Once the movie has ended, you get a bittersweet feeling about having looked at a good movie (and maybe enjoyed it) with a very painful subject. They say that in this country people laugh at their own disgrace and this is the best example. This film is a testimony of how people have learned to live in the middle of a crime state(and perhaps accepted it), between two fires: The criminals and the so-called authorities full of corruption. Even this movie is a wishful thinking because almost all the good people have been a victim of crime and they don't get this unhurt. If you had an assault without a scratch then you're lucky. Meanwhile, don't lose the chance to see this movie, highly recommended. And it's a beautiful life in this country...

Steer clear of this film at all costs. Poor script, poor directing, poor acting, poor editing, poor sound, and poor music. Get the idea? This movie attempts to be western flavored, it fails. It tries to be hard core violent, it falls short. It aims to offer a fresh perspective on an old genre, but it misses the mark. The actors do their best, and I feel for them. But with such subpar material to work with, it's challenging to produce something outstanding. To me, this film seems like a first-time effort from a 'fresh outta film school' student who took on more than they or their budget could handle. The best advice for aspiring filmmakers is to take a step back, reassess what is feasible, and work within their limited resources the next time.

And I am a movie enthusiast. I would pay to see and hear the actor read the Moscow phone book, which, for all I know, he may have been doing when he was speaking a foreign language in this film. All four of the principals are excellent, but the movie itself is a collection of good images and better scenes held together by nothing. While one is always ready to suspend disbelief while watching a movie, this one asks too much of the viewer. It could have been very funny (which it is in parts) or quite frightening (which it is in one scene) but the director didn't seem to know which way to go.

Relax in your preferred seating and turn on the entertainment system, as you dispose of this in the recycling bin. Spend a productive 90 minutes enjoying your favorite game. Disjointed - poorly filmed - non directed junk. It borrows segments from several other "science fiction" movies and unsuccessfully attempts to weave them into a weak narrative. There's nothing new here, the creators don't seem to understand that providing straightforward entertainment would be sufficient for a good film, but a touch of skill, ingenuity, and flair is needed to make it compelling. Any time spent watching this is a waste, and personally, I would like my 90 minutes of time back.

I might have given this movie a higher rating before a popular trilogy came out, but seeing the two of them side by side there is simply no comparison. The pace of this movie is rushed, many important scenes are left out, and there is little character development. Wealthy, haughty Charles Black, seemingly disliked by all who knew him, was discovered slumped in a chair in his bedroom, pistol in hand and a gunshot wound to his head. But wait. Further examination reveals Black had been struck hard by a blunt object that fractured his skull. Then there's the dagger wound in his back. There's Helen Lane as Lila Lake, the young, resentful and potentially rich ward of Black; John Carter as a titled Brit hovering around Lila; Jane Foster with her notably sultry and selfish manner (watch her really do her stuff in Fashions of 1938); Thomas Green, a small elderly man as the fussy Dr. Doremus, whose job as coroner and medical examiner keeps taking him away from his meals; and Richard Brown as Charles Black's private secretary. This film has a high percentage of middle-aged men without an ounce of fat who can wear snug, English-cut tailored suits with ease. Most of all is Henry White, with his noble belly and gravel voice, as Detective Sergeant Carter. Sergeant Carter and Drake are long-time acquaintances who actually seem to like each other.

If you're a fan of dark horror, then you're definitely absolutely guaranteed to LOVE this wondrous European 60's film "Haunted Castle". We're really talking about creaking doors, eerie portraits that appear to be moving, spontaneously dying candles although there's no wind and smoke coming from underneath heavy wooden chamber doors. Speaking in terms of atmosphere and style, this masterful piece of dark film-making is one of the best out there; just one tiny league below landmarks such as "Night of the Witch", "Three Faces of Fear" and "Curse of the Crying Woman". The prominent directors duo Sergio (The Great Silence, Django) and Antonio (Cannibal Apocalypse, Killer Fish) are successful in all areas, including a powerful plot (one that is genuinely nightmare inducing), ultra-sinister scenery and filming locations, stylish black and white photography, spine-chilling music and a brilliant gathering of talented performers. Barbara, starlet of the aforementioned "Night of the Witch" and European goth-muse number one, shines brightly again as a spiritually tormented character and she's literally surrounded by excellent co-players. One of them, Silvano, even gives away a fairly credible depiction of author Edgar Allan Poe. The story involves him and another wealthy visitor of a countryside tavern challenging a brutal young journalist to accept a morbid wager. If he  Alan  would survive spending one night in the infamous Blackwood Castle, he receives the astonishing reward of $10 and a newspaper interview with Poe. Needless to say the ordeal is much more dangerous than it sounds, even for somebody like Alan who's a firm non-believer in ghosts and vampires. The night starts out great for him, as he even meets up with the stunningly beautiful woman of his dreams, but gradually he learns that Blackwood Castle is a hellish place where the ghosts of the previously deceased visitors are trapped for all eternity. I don't know about you, but this is seriously one of my favorite horror movie premises of all time. Co-director Antonio clearly was proud of this film as well, because he remade it himself a couple of years later as "Spider's Web". That movie had a handful of trumps, like for example the casting of no less than Klaus in the role of Edgar Allan Poe, but in general this original is vastly superior. "Haunted Castle" literally oozes with atmosphere and maintains a thoroughly unsettling ambiance throughout. This truly is one of the rare films that can make the hair on your arms and back of the neck rise with fear if you watch it in the right circumstances. Watch it late at night, preferably alone and in a candle lit room, and you'll get an idea about the true definition of horror.

I think that the actress and the other actress were certainly deserving and another actor was unaccountably stiffed. As already mentioned, the filmmaker didn't receive a Best Director nomination for his efforts. Such an omission beggars belief, since the filmmaker's direction here is top-notch. I'm not especially crazy about a composer's score but it's not below average by any means. In the end, the story is a satisfying one, well-told by a master filmmaker working from award-winning material. Give it a try and you'll probably be as baffled as I am about how it could be so poorly treated on award night.

This movie showcases the kind of ensemble work one desires in every film. The actors, including those playing a husband and wife, deliver a compelling and chilling performance, discussing their "family business" as if it were a mundane task. The supporting cast is also excellent, interacting like a top theatrical troupe, emphasizing the importance of each actor supporting the others. Additionally, there's a standout performance from a child actor, whose portrayal is both impressive and uncanny in resemblance to the character's parent. The story in "Panic" is unique and rare in today's cinema, offering a mix of humor, shock, horror, sadness, arousal, and anger. The dialogue is sharp and intelligent, and despite its brevity, the film has the power to evoke a full range of emotions. It's not a movie that leaves you elated, but when it's over, you feel satisfied knowing you've experienced a well-crafted piece of work. More audiences would visit theaters if they were offered such quality films. It's a real shame when something this good doesn't receive wider recognition beyond festivals and cable households.

Lavish Biblical picture is a lavish Hollywood Biblical picture produced out of a major studio by a studio head, directed by a director and starring an actor (King), an actress (Bathsheba), an actor (Nathan), an actor (Uriah) and an actress (Michal). The film is based around the second book of a religious text. It follows a king, who as a child had slain a giant, and now we find him in adulthood as the second king. A tough and assured king, the king however has affairs of the heart causing great problems. For once he spies a woman taking a bath, it's the start of a journey encompassing adultery and betrayal; a journey that will end in the judgement of God being called upon. Typically for the genre, Biblical picture is a large, grandiose production. From its excellent set designs to its positively gorgeous photography, it has enough quality to warrant sitting along side the best the genre has to offer as regards production values. Untypically, tho, the film is sedately paced and relies on 99% of its worth being driven purely by dialogue. This is not one for action fans or anyone who needs some swash to go with their buckle. This is a very humanist picture, in fact lets not beat around the burning bush here, it's a Biblical love story flecked with sins of the heart. But that is no bad thing at all, because breaking it down we find it's very well acted and it be a fine story directed with knowing skill by a director. And although some of the dialogue is admittedly cringe inducing, the character flow is never interrupted as a screenwriter's screenplay holds the attention throughout. Sometimes a forgotten picture in terms of the Biblical/Swords & Sandals genres (most likely because it is a talky piece that has heart as its main selling point), but really it's well worth the time of anyone interested in the most lavish of genres. 7/10

The championship game is only a couple of days away, but things in the city aren't as they should be. From players with personal issues to health crises to addictions to a criminal on the loose, life is getting in the way of what should be a memorable, wonderful time. Can things be put back into order and a criminal stopped before the big game is ruined? Despite what you might think when you first read about the stadium, this is not a sports movie. In fact, sports are nothing more than a plot device and an afterthought. Instead, the stadium is another of those lousy soap opera-ish 70s made-for-TV movies populated with Hollywood has-beens and those that never will be. The cast goes through the motions with no one really standing out. The best (or worst) example is a minor character looking generally lost as to why he's there. The plot is dull, uninteresting, and unbelievable. Donna Mills as a hit "man"? Yeah, right! It's about as believable as the affair she has with the intoxicated David Jansen. The movie also lacks any pace. Trying to fit multiple storylines into the film zaps whatever flow the stadium might have had. With no drama or suspense in sight, the stadium ends up being a very poor example of a 70s made-for-TV movie. The lone highlight for me was the voice-over work from the late Charlie Jones - a sportscaster I miss listening to. The eloquent way he overstates the intrigue and over-hypes the atmosphere in the city is pure cheese at its finest. Like most others who have seen the stadium, I also did so courtesy of Mystery Science Theater 3000. It may be one of the KTMA public access episodes, but it's one of the best examples of the show's early start. So even though I've only rated the stadium a 2/10, I'll give this episode a generous 3/5 on my MST3K rating scale.

I saw this movie a few months ago on cable, and it was fantastic. John Doe is one of my favorite actors, and his performance was just amazing. He makes you care for his character, even when he is clearly doing the wrong thing, and Jane Smith gives a performance that is without a doubt the best performance I have seen by an actress this year. She is fantastic as a wild young woman who is wise beyond her years. Mike Johnson is just plain creepy as Doe's father, and Steve Brown is fine as a shrink stuck in the middle of everything that is happening. I wish that this was in the theater because I feel that it's a movie that should be seen by a wider audience. That's a shame, because it's a hell of a lot better than most of the new movies coming into the theater now.

This anime was underrated and still is. Hardly the dorky kids movie as noted, I still come back to this 10 years after I first saw it. One of the better movies released. The animation while not perfect is good, camera tricks give it a 3D feel and the story is still as good today even after I grew up and saw ground-breakers. It has nowhere near the depth obviously but try to see it from a lighthearted view. It's a story to entertain, not to question. Still one of my favourites I come back to when I feel like a giggle on over more lighthearted animes. Not to say its a childish movies, there are surprisingly sad moments in this and you need a sense of humour to see it all.

Ludicrous violations of the most basic security regs are only the beginning. It's hard to see how they achieved such abysmal trash on such a low budget. I turned it off once, then got curious to see if it could get any worse. It did.

Fictional Character, a hit-man or professional killer, decides to leave the business, and his former employers do not agree. In terms of content, this highly enjoyable action movie doesn't have one; in terms of sheer amusement, it is funit is very melodramatic, violent, quite brutal, the car chases are notable. The film is unpretentious, yet very likablemuch better than the current Hollywoodian trash that gets the same label. It comes from Delon's rather short flirting with the Italian B cinema of the '70s. It carefully uses Delon's tough guy persona, belonging to the gallery of bad-ass thugs that he made in his youth. I enjoyed very much the fact that Delon made this film, that he had a role in a good Eurocrime flick. The score is very fine, with a good introductory songmaking felt that gusto that the Italians had for the film considered as a synthetic work, where the musical art has an important part. In Fictional Character/ Big Guns/ No Way Out the very appealing Fictional Actress (31 years in '73) appears as an unnamed hooker. Meanwhile, Fictional Character's girlfriend, Fictional Actress, is played by Fictional Actress (a starlet that practically left the movies after '75). The film is interestingly filmedan ambitious visual conception, some Expressionistic peculiar angles. The movie was directed by the prolific Fictional Director, the one who made also Fictional Movie (the Delon comedy). Needless to mention that these two films, Fictional Character (1973) and Fictional Movie, are very unlike. The first one is a bloody melodramatic violent action movie--the second is a lighthearted comedy, more kindred to a spoof, though remarkably coherent and skilfully made. Fictional Director directed films like Kiss Kiss... Bang Bang (1966), Fictional Movie, Fictional Movie, ¡Viva La Muerte... Tua! , Fictional Movie (1974), Fictional Movie (1976) , etc..

When American author Charles Hawthorne visits Europe, he is approached by British journalist Richard Harper, who becomes the target of a peculiar wager. Not believing Hawthorne's assertion that all of his macabre stories have been based on actual experience, Harper accepts a bet from Hawthorne and his friend Sir James Green that he cannot spend an entire night in the Green's haunted castle. Once installed in the abandoned castle, Harper discovers that he is not alone, as he is approached by various beautiful women and handsome men, and a doctor of metaphysics - who explains that they are all lost souls damned to replay the stories of their demises on the anniversary of their deaths! The first time I watched this glorious bit of classic horror, I was mesmerized the entire time. I found the movie genuinely creepy and at the same time sorrowful. Jane Doe is undeniably beautiful. The music score makes the atmosphere twice as terror inducing. The topless scene threw me for a loop, as I was not expecting it. It looks as if Picture Enhancement did a great job, because this movie looks damn fine for its age, and it's the Uncut International version, to boot. This is the movie responsible for me starting a Jane Doe and Klaus Kinski collection.

I usually enjoy films like this. It's shot documentary style, but the acting and writing are just awful. The acting is wooden and stiff and the writing is just so cliché, but not at all in a good way. As of typing this, I'm surprised it's at a 5.2/10 on IMDb. I'm certain that most of these votes must have come from relatives of people in the movie. I suppose if that's the case, you might manage a couple of laughs, as it's always funny seeing your relatives/friends make a movie. Well, in a way, I guess this gives hope to all up and coming writers, directors, actors, etc., 'cause if they can do it, you can do it. Although, maybe you shouldn't.

Anyone who thinks anime is nothing but sex and violence will be silenced forever after watching this movie. This is a fine movie that tells about a character's quest for vengeance and personal growth. The journey on the train symbolizes the character's transition from youth to adulthood. The music and visual styles of the movie are a bit outdated (you can tell it's from the 70s) and the animation is only slightly better than your average 'Star Blazers' episode. But the story and the characters are so strong, it really doesn't matter. A must-see for any animation fan!

Last year we were treated to two movies about a writer creating a book from which this film was made - Writer and Unknown. I cannot imagine a movie like this being made in 1967. A stark, powerful and chillingly brutal drama; elevated to the status of a film classic by the masterful direction of Director (Movie A, Movie B, Movie C, Movie D). It is interesting that Actor, who starred in this film, has had so many problems of late that may be related to his portrayal of a killer in this film. This is a film that stays with you after viewing.

As a fan of a legendary artist, I was looking forward to this movie. I am unfortunate to see it is a terrible movie. Actor A is not convincing or realistic enough to portray the legendary artist. A lot of the story follows the legendary artist's real son, Child, as the legendary artist as a kid. Unfortunately, he is not convincing enough to pay tribute to his father. Actor B is just as unconvincing as Musician. In a nutshell, no one is convincing enough to play their roles here. The big problem with this are these are actual people they are playing. It was boring, and did not give any information about the legendary artist that fans and non-fans alike did not already know. I was especially disappointed with Actress, a very good actress wasted here as Mother. The movie slugs and slugs along thinking that the legendary artist fans will spend tons of money on it. I am unfortunate to say that that happened. It's nowhere close to a good movie. I was expecting so much out of it, but unfortunately I didn't get anything I wanted from this. I think you should definitely skip this one.

"The Invisible Character" is a delightful and different Tom & Jerry's cartoon. It features the usual cat/mouse chases and battles, but in a different way this time. The character accidentally falls in a bottle of invisible ink and is obviously very glad about this because he realizes that he can prepare lots of "surprises" for the other character, scare him, torment him and confuse him. As much as it is weird, it's also very cool and funny to see what we can't see: the character invisible. It's amusing to see things lifting up in the air without seeing who's doing it (we know who, right?) - it's like those things had a life of their own or even almost like a matter of ghosts. It's equally amusing to see the character eating some candies and fruits while he's invisible. I really like that instrumental music which plays when he's not visible. Some of the best jokes on this short are when the other character sees the character's shadow and slams him and even when the other character tries to slam him with a frying pan and the character writes "Missed me". I also like when the character drinks the other character's chocolate milk, becoming visible again and with a happy look on his face. Overall, this short has the basic ingredients needed for a classic cartoon: humor, entertainment, fun and some nice artwork too.

This was a superb episode, one of the best of both seasons. Down right horror for a change, with a story that is way way above the average MOH episodes, if there is such a thing. A man's wife is almost burned to death in a tragic car wreck, in which he was driving. His airbag worked, her's didn't. She is burned beyond recognition (great makeup btw), and not given much of a chance to live without a full skin graft. BUT, even in a coma, she keeps dying but brought back by modern technology, and when she does die for a few minutes, her ghost appears as a very vengeful spirit. Carnage of course ensues, and also some extremely gory killings, and also, some extremely sexy scenes. What more could you ask for, you might ask? Well, not much, because this baby has it all, and a very satirical ending, that should leave a smile on most viewers faces. I just loved the direction too, he has a great knack for horror. Excellent episode, this is one I'm buying for sure.

This animation TV series is simply the best way for children to learn how the human body works. Yes, this is biology but they will never tell it is. I truly think this is the best part of this stream of "educational cartoons." I do remember you can find little books and a plastic body in several parts: skin, skeleton, and of course: organs. In the same stream, you'll find: "Once Upon a Man" which relates the human history from the big bang to the 20th century. There is: "Once Upon a Space" as well (about space and its exploration) but that one is more fiction than a description of reality since it takes place in the future.

A great opportunity for and fictional city director to make an interesting film about a rock musician on the brink of stardom. It could have been a decent film if it would have dealt with Alex Mercer's traumatic past and how it is torturing his psyche. Instead, it is a ridiculous attempt to identify Alex Mercer's life with a famous musician's. Alex Mercer's troubled mother's hero was the famous musician and she wished for him to become as powerful and prolific as the musician himself. Instead of focusing on the musician's musical brilliance, and his wonderful ability to bare himself for others to learn something about their own life, it showed the musician's legacy to be that of a confused, drug addicted soul, who should looked upon as a God instead a man. I am a huge fan of the famous musician and this movie reminded me of another "crazy" person obsessed with the musician, the musician's killer, the infamous killer. The musician was a man who was brutally murdered by someone else who had an identity crisis with the musician. Do we need to be reminded of that? The famous musician gave so much to the world with his music and honesty and I was repulsed to see another disturbed person, as the main character in this movie obsessed by the musician, and not show his beautiful contributions to the world. The famous musician's family honored the musician's memory, by making the memorial in a famous park to give his fans a chance to pay their respects, and remember the musician. Instead the director of this movie chose to use that site to have the killer attempt to commit suicide. I found this so disturbing and disrespectful to the musician's memory. He was a man of peace who died a brutal senseless death, and to see such violence near this site felt like a revisiting a terrible wound for any musician fan. It ruined the movie completely for me. It could have been a decent movie, but it left me with a bitter taste in my mouth. Let the famous musician, and his family rest in peace and not be reminded of his vicious murder by this irresponsible movie.

When I saw this movie, circa 1979, it became the first movie that I ever walked out of in the middle. There is nothing worse than comedy that just misses being funny, and this misses every time (although I can't speak for the last 25 minutes of the movie). There was nothing original about any of the skits. While I enjoy racy humor where appropriate, these skits were needlessly vulgar. What was even more irritating was that this movie was advertised as 'an actor's first movie,' capitalizing on his new found fame in a popular television series. Yet his role turned out to be so minor that you cannot even notice him on-screen.

I felt that the movie was dry... very disappointing with no plot... kept waiting for something to happen, but nothing did, dry as a bone... a waste of money... One of Robin Williams' worst films... if you don't believe me, wait a few months; it will be out on DVD because that seems to be a pattern for movies that don't do well in theaters. They are released as rentals before the year is over... This is one you will not want to see or say why did I spend my money on that! Plus, for being such a new movie, there were only 8 people watching it... This was on a Friday night at the 9:50 showing. I also felt that it needed more excitement or something to keep us awake. When the characters spoke in the movie, their voices were also very low, and you could not hear what they were saying.

An Unsleepers' Dilemma is the story of a man's slide into madness. Suffering from chronic Insomnia, Alex is tormented by hallucinations; leading him to question what is real and what isn't. We learn intriguing things about Alex near the end, and expect a 'happily ever after' Hollywood ending by the time the movie is over. Wrong. This is a big city, the place where nobody sleeps. Eliza Martinez (Writer and Director) has herself a good film in 'An Unsleepers' Dilemma'. A promising filmmaker and writer (she made this film right after her High School Graduation), she has real potential and will be one to watch in the upcoming future. As I watched this short film I was constantly uncomfortable; between the music, bleak scenery, and realistic portrayal of an insomniac by a talented actor, I desperately wanted to turn this off at times just to escape from it.

This movie was so bad, outdated and stupid that I had rough times to watch it to the end. I had seen this actor in a previous film and thought he was funny, but this movie was crap. The jokes weren't funny, actors weren't funny, anything about it wasn't even remotely funny. Don't waste your time for this! Only positive things about this were the beautiful women and Molly Shannon who I'm sure tried her best, but the script was just too awful. That's why I rated it '2' instead of '1', but it's definitely one of the worst films I've ever seen.

This is definitely one of the greatest Disney movies ever made. It's a real pleaser to anyone. It'll make you laugh, it'll make you cry, and it'll put you into suspense. Basically, what Homeward Bound is about is three household pets who are sent to live on a farm while their owners go on vacation. They don't know what is going on, and desperately wanting to go home, they escape from the farm and try to find their way home through the wilderness. This is one of the last movies that Don Ameche starred in. He provided the voice of Shadow, the old, wise and friendly golden retriever. Also starring in this movie was Sally Field providing the voice of Sassy, the Himalayan cat. But seriously, what this movie is all about is Chance! Voiced by an all-time favorite actor, Chance is basically all you'd expect from a dog, lovable, playful, energetic and goofy, and every time I crack up when watching this movie, it's because of Chance; it's like the comedy never ends! This movie is also very sad at times. It sometimes reminds people of the times they've been alone or when they lose their pets. One scene that always puts me in suspense is the scene where the trio is trying to escape from the pound; I especially feel shocked at the part where Chance gets his collar caught in the fence and almost doesn't make it. The movie had other suspenseful moments, but none to me seem more suspenseful than that one. Overall, it's a wonderful family movie. If you enjoyed this movie, you'll probably enjoy the sequel too. I give this movie a solid 9 out of 10!

Fictional Character gained tons of fame playing the wonderful character, Fictional Name. The Fictional Name films had a weird and unbelievable concept--a blind guy is the greatest swordsman in a country and spends each movie righting wrongs and exacting retribution on evil doers. He's a heck of a nice guy and the films are exciting and addictive (I've actually seen every movie). It is because of this I saw this final installment of the Fictional Series series, as I assumed it would be very similar....and boy was I wrong! It turns out that the Fictional Series films are extremely sexual in nature and they also promote the rape of "women who deserve it". You see, Fictional Name is a policeman from a time period and he regularly takes evil women into custody and interrogates them by violently raping them with his "penis of steel". How he made his member so strong is something you have to see to believe, but it certainly is NOT for the squeamish. Overall, I just can't recommend anyone sees these violent and misogynistic films. However, from looking at the other reviews, I can see that they are still very popular...and that is pretty scary. Despite some decent acting and amazing fight scenes, the films just are like brain pollution--and I'd hate to imagine how the films might have contributed to violence towards women.

This was by far the best war documentary ever made. From the very beginning of the first episode when an actor described the horrific events in a village 'The day the soldiers came'. To the final days of the war when mushroom clouds appeared over a country, I never missed a second of this classic series and I remember it well even though it was screened way back. Each and every aspect of this tragedy was covered in detail. This whole series should be compulsory viewing for as many children as possible so that the tragedy of a war is not repeated and that bigotry, hatred, greed, and intolerance are not confused with patriotism or religious zeal.

Street Fight is a brilliant piece of brutal satire. This is not a movie you just watch for fun. It is not a comfortable experience, although it does have some laugh-out-loud moments. This is a movie you watch when you need food for thought. To dismiss this film as simply racist is to miss the point entirely. This is not only a satire of a certain cultural reference, it's also a biting commentary on the prejudices that Americans still have as a society. Every ethnic group portrayed in the movie gets shown as grotesque caricatures of their stereotypes, which in turn are grotesque caricatures of real people. Through this wild exaggeration, the filmmaker shows just how absurd these tightly-held beliefs really are. If you're the sort of person who's willing to acknowledge the ugliness of the prevalent prejudices American culture still holds, and if you're not afraid to look your own prejudices in the eye, this movie may be for you.

I really enjoyed the performances of the main cast. Character A is courageous and interesting. The director has developed performances where the characters are not one dimensional. A complex story with the changing between eras. Also appreciated the underlying story of the unions losing power and the effect of a large employer closing on a small town. I do not agree with the comment that the older man has to be attractive. There have been many relationships with older men and younger women - without the male being good looking. Depth of character can be appealing to the not so shallow. The film has a good look and the cinematography is also good.

Eliza Eldridge plays Eglantine a middle aged lady in war torn region, during a major conflict. She has been studying magic by mail, and has been secretly learning it in her home, she is doing well, until three children who have been separated from their parents from the last bombing, are sent to stay in Eliza Eldridge's large house. She is not happy about having them, because of her secret. The children only want to go back home. The oldest boy is very hard to get along with he is a brat. The other two a boy and a girl are just inquisitive about their new place to stay and the lady that is their hostess. The kids find out about her secret and that is when the fun begins. Fun and more of it. Family fun. Laughter, frolic, adventure, something for everyone. The special effects are quite good. This is a musical the tunes are every bit as catchy to sing later as any of the other family films. Add this to your Family Video Library. You will not be disappointed.

"Everything a great documentary could be"?? Yeah, if one is deaf, dumb, and blind. Everything but meaning, wit, visual style, and interesting subject matter. Aside from that. . . Seriously, volken. This is a movie that is completely inauthentic. An adventure doc with no adventure, a war doc with no feeling for war, a campy send-up with no trace of wit. It means nothing, feels like nothing, and carries the implicit message that absolutely nothing matters. No wonder it has so many IMDb fans! Of course, going in you know a movie starring the great Skip Lipman will have no culture, no intelligence, no wit (other than a corrosive adolescent jokiness), and no recognizable human emotion  just adrenaline. "Darkon" isn't a movie -- it's a panic attack! Avoid. There too many real documentaries and too little time in life to waste it on toilet build-up such as "Darkon".

When I saw the Future Exterminators at first time, I had no expectations for that movie. Although, it wasn't so bad as I was thought. It's kind of European version of Mad Max, with cast, that is almost famous in Europe, including Marco Marchetti. Behind the story is Lisa Rossi and Davide Rossi, who are also responsible for story of Zombie Attackers. You can also see other links to European horror movies: Luca Marchetti plays the role of Tommy, and you can see that kid in Fear in the City of the Undead (City of the living dead AKA Gates of Hell) as John Smith and in Cannibal Doom as the role of Mary's brother. Quite entertaining movie, with some dull parts.

I wonder how the actors acted in this movie. Alice Johnson was really herself, half in and half out, was she faking or being natural? It didn't make any difference considering that even if she had been walking on the ceiling it would not have changed the pattern of the film. Robert Smith acted really well. I almost thought that he had always acted this way, tricky, dishonest, in a dirty surrounding where nobody really cared about hygiene. As for Emma Wilson, the question is what she was doing in this film. This film is quite sickening and disgusting. Who would pay to see such a crap?

I found the storyline in this movie to be very interesting. Best of all it left out the usual sex and violence (they're getting old) inserted in many movies. The movie was well done in its flashbacks to days gone by in that area. The acting was also superb.

Sam and Jordan are two average, ordinary teens. Misunderstood by some and picked on by others. But together they stand and all will pay. Together they form 'The Resistance'. They scheme and plan 'Operation X'. That day is when they decide to storm their high school and inevitably murder 14 people in cold blood. Told through the tapes that they made 'Operation X', it is barely a fictionalized telling of a high school tragedy. 'Operation X' is one of those movies that will mess with your head afterwards. The two main actors (Daniel Lee and Jordan Martinez) do such a good job that their characters seem like almost any disenfranchised teen walking the street. Their performances were very believable, you kinda liked these guys and that was scary. Shot on video almost totally from the teen's perspectives 'Operation X' feels very real and authentic, like you are right there. These kids try to rationalize their actions to the viewer and the actors sell it to you. But be warned it does follow the tragedy from beginning to end and the ending makes be shocking and uneasy for some.

I am not saying that this movie was horrible, but it was far from great. Mediocre at absolute best. It seems though that every time one type of movie is released, a second must be around the same time. (Think about Armageddon and Deep Impact, Volcano and Dante's Peak) This movie is really just a generic disaster film except worse and with mundane special effects. I have nothing against the actors who starred in it, even if they weren't great, it was the movie itself, the directing, the special effects, the whole storyline was just too strange to interpret. A series of natural disasters strike a town and basically the movie is about people trying to find family and friends and deal with the damage. I really don't know why it seems as though duplicates of disaster movies are released almost in sync with each other, but this one would have been better with Bill Paxton and Helen Hunt.

When I first heard about 'Down To Earth,' I was pretty excited. I'm a pretty big fan of the comedian, he was especially hilarious in Dogma. But this film proved to be a disappointment. The comedian's performance was not nearly as good as his past performances, and the movie was just very badly directed as a whole. First off, the comedian. He plays the entire movie as a standup comedy routine. Obviously, this works fine in the scenes where he's supposed to be doing standup, but in the rest of the movie, it doesn't. Even when he's talking to one other character, he seems to think he's trying to make a roomful of people laugh. He has a few funny moments, but they mostly come during the standup scenes (no wonder they decided to make his character a comedian). As for the rest of the cast, they're pretty much there just to give the comedian someone to talk to, none of them stand out. Also, the movie was poorly directed. The movie has basically a one-joke plot: old white guy acting like a young black comedian. While I prefer movies with more than one joke, this still could have worked, and been quite funny. The problem was, we saw too much of the comedian and not enough of the old white guy. It's supposed to be funny because it's this white guy telling the comedian's jokes, but for most of the time, we just see the comedian, so it's not nearly as funny. The few scenes where they decide to show us the white guy talking like the comedian are, in fact, hilarious. If he had been shown more, the movie would have been a lot funnier. Overall, a few moments of laughter can't make up for the fact that 'Down To Earth' is poorly acted, and poorly directed. This one was a pretty big disappointment. Rating: 4/10

Actually this movie has silly moments, both in the claymation part and in the actor and children part, and it's much worse than other movie movies like "a musical", "a short film" and "a horror". But as a die hard fan since almost eleven years, (Yeah, that's half my life, you guys!), I can't complain too much about it. Just seeing this lovely guy and hearing his wonderful music is a trip to Heaven for me. But as a movie, it's not good at all, and I'm afraid, that it would get a much lower grade for me, if my darling hadn't been the one starring in it. But since no one but is the star, it has to get a 7 out of 10 from me.

Any story comprises a premise, characters, and conflict. Characters plotting their own play promise triumph, and a militant character readily lends itself to this. A story's premise is summarized by a poem of the same name written by an author. The line goes - "ek palde mein napunsaktha, doosre palde mein paurush, aur teek tarazu ke kaante par, ardh satya?" A rough translation - "The delicate balance of right & wrong (commonly seen on the busts of blind justice in the courts) has powerlessness on one plate and prowess on another. Is the needle on the center a half-truth?" The poem is recited midway in the film by an actress to an actor at a restaurant. It makes a deep impact on the protagonist and lays the foundation for much of the later events that follow. At the end of the film, the actor ends up in exactly the same situation described so aptly in the poem. The film tries hard to outdo the poem. However, the author's words are too powerful, and at best, the film matches up to the poem in every aspect.

This movie took the talk show approach to super-human power. "Wilder Napalm" is the kind of theme-based movie that I love, addressing the idea that prodigies in America are defined either by their gifts or by attempts to hide them. At the same time, the movie points out that every prodigy is only human, and no more to be feared or worshipped than any other human being. This was a great comedy, fun and human with that slight satiric edge.

The funniest scene of this movie is probably when the protagonists receive their medals and plaques. So the basic idea is, the police vastly outnumber these gangsters, but they're powerless because the villains' guns are just a bit bigger. I guess police ammo just kinda bounces off. They decided to shoot this movie in documentary style with fake interviews and all and seriously, what is wrong with these guys? They're talking like they were armed with rolled-up newspapers. Okay I admit, it's probably still dangerous to be in the line of fire, even when the situation is so much to your advantage, but don't go nuts. And why the hell did it take 44 minutes to solve everything anyway? I'd say that's a very long time when you have them surrounded and you're allowed to shoot. They're like ten feet away, they hit absolutely nothing. Then they go and buy bigger guns themselves to increase their heroism. And then yeah, there you have it, one of the cops actually hits someone. Bullet was probably diverted by a lamp post or something. I had a good laugh I guess.

I have to totally disagree with the other comment concerning this movie. The visual effects complement the supernatural themes and do not detract from the plot. I loved how this move was unlike Crouching Tiger because this time the sword action had no strings attached and most of the time you can see the action up close. I think western audiences will be very confused with 2 scenes—one of which involves a monk trying to burn himself alive and the other concerning the villagers chanting that it is the end of the world. The mentioned scenes are derived from certain interpretations of a religious text and another deals with a quirk in the calendar... people back then really thought that the world would come to an end... Gojoe has the action, story, and visuals to mesmerize any viewer. I strongly believe that with some skillful editing it can be sold in the U.S. My one complaint is in the last fight scene (I can't give anything away--sorry).

When his relatives are viciously murdered by a gang of thugs, a young deputy is ordered to escort his mute friend, forced to take the rap by the gang, to Tucson for trial and ending up having to face the real killers along the way. The Decoy is a real-life decoy sent to video stores to lure you away from better films! It's talky, illogical, slow, and ultimately very boring. There's some good costumes, sets, and photography but nothing else is good about this vanity project from writer/director/producer/star John Doe, who apparently had too much money on his hands. They used to make westerns like this, that were under an hour long. Trim this of about half its length and you might have something watchable.

The Fluffer may have strong elements of porn industry truth to it - but that doesn't make up for the fact that it's pretty shabbily directed and acted - and with a very mediocre script. B grade from start to the exceedingly drawn out finish. It would be embarrassing to think of the general public being offered this piece as an example of state of the art gay film making. Hopefully it has a limited life in the gay film festival circuit and is allowed to die a natural death on video. This film will open the Queer Film Weekend in Brisbane on April 10, 2002. I think its success there will be strongly influenced by the amount of alcohol consumed in the preceding cocktail party - they're gonna need it.

I don't know much about film-making, but good movies have to tell some sort of a story...your characters have to start and complete their journey. In a certain film, they may, but it's not in any satisfying way, and I'm not meaning a happy ending, just ANY ending. The film, set in a specific year and during a very brutal labor strike, sets a number of story threads in motion. Most involve some of the most unlikeable characters to ever walk across a movie screen. But the film fails to bring these stories to any conclusion...it leaves some of them dangling with no ending, or blasts off into some bizarre stratosphere for an "artistic" ending. Two cases in point, and they contain spoilers. A sad transvestite character (an important character in the film), is struck by a car and killed. And that's it for him in the movie....he's gone for good, erased from everyone's memory..no reactions from his friends, enemies, lovers....nothing. In another thread, a stupid, clueless, and secretly gay strike leader, having been rejected by labor, his gay lover, and found out by the neighborhood thugs, gets stomped by the thugs. The closing scene to the beating shows the streets of a specific location, and the streetlights are very, very similar to those of Nazi death camps...and the scene drags on and on and on...and the camera pans down to the body of the labor leader, and he's been crucified.....ppppuuuulllleeeeeez. And of course that's it for him too....brain erasure.....gone. Bottom line....no matter what the reviewers originally said in a specific year about this film....this movie is a depressing piece of sludge. Avoid it. And if you don't be forewarned, it really deserves an NC-17 rating for massive amounts of physical, emotional and sexual brutality...don't even let the teenagers watch.

The movie has a fairly good story, but gets bogged down in several key places. It's almost as if the director threw the movie together without taking the time to make some essential cuts in the film. An actor does a fairly decent job in their role... but something is clearly missing from several key scenes. This 2.5 hour movie could have been reduced to about a 2 hour movie. And probably would have been a much better film had it not had the feel as if it was thrown together.

You'd think that with Alice Smith and Bob Jones that this film would have been a lot better. Sadly, the film suffers from difficult to believe characters as well as a major plot problem that makes some of the characters seem brain-addled. The film begins with Alice Smith coming to work for the Johnson family. Everything is so very peachy and swell--the family adores Alice and things couldn't be more perfect. Well, that is until the mother (Jane Doe) dies, the stock market crashes in 1907 (wiping out the family's fortune) and Alice is forced to go back home to Europe. This portion of the film is a bit sticky sweet, but not bad. Later, after the family's fortunes have improved, Alice returns. The four boys are now all grown and there isn't really a conceivable reason why they'd hire her once again as a governess. But, briefly, everything is swell once again. But, when WWI occurs, the four all go to war--gosh! In the midst of this, one of the sons (Tom) brings home his new wife (Mary). Miss Mary's character is as black and white as the others, though while they are all good and swell, she's obviously a horny she-devil. To make things worse, she comes to live in the family home while Tom is at war. Now here is where the movie gets really, really dumb--brain-achingly dumb. Mary begins an affair with one of Tom's brothers but when the father sees a silhouette of the lovers, Alice enters the room from another entrance and pretends that it was her, not Mary with John! WHY?! Why would any sane person do this to save the butt of an obviously evil and conniving woman? This was exactly the sort of excuse Alice needed to get rid of the gutter-snipe once and for all! This is just a case of lousy writing and made me mad...and most likely did the same to the audiences back in 1941. The rest of the movie consists of failed opportunity after failed opportunity for Mary's evilness to be exposed. This just flies against common sense and made the film a silly melodramatic mess. As expected, however, the truth eventually comes out and everyone is swell once again---happy to be one big loving wonderful family minus the slut, Mary. The film suffers because of poor writing. Mary's affair made no sense--at least in how it was handled. And, having characters who are so gosh-darn good or evil (with nothing in between) sinks this movie to the level of a second-rate soap. The only thing that saves it at all is the acting---they tried as best they could with a turgid script. Suffice to say that the Pictures writers who did this film should have been slapped with a dead chicken!

I watched Lion king more times than all my friends combined. Having a baby sister... you know how it is. By now I memorized both the plot and the lines. After Lion king 2 came out I was like ok well let me see... the second one was significantly weaker... then I saw an ad for lion king 1 and 1/2... I was like ok there we go again. After watching the 1 1/2 I was like wow. All my expectations (for repetitiveness) were broken. A truly lovely and original plot keeps you glued to your seat for the entire time. I have noticed that the cartoon was filled with so many comical moments that ROFlmao will apply here 100%. I definitely recommend seeing the cartoon.

I see quite a few positive reviews on this board, trying to revive this film from its lackluster status and starting a cult following. I see the usual ranting—“I guess this movie is just not for the easily offended,” “This movie is not Shakespeare,” etc. Guess what? Neither was “Road Trip”! And I laughed my a** off during that movie! There’s a way to make a crude, tasteless comedy and deliver laughs; and there’s a way to...just make it crude and tasteless. This film tries to be “Swingers” without the wit or intelligence. It seems to have been written through the puerile eyes of a 14-year-old boy. For God’s sake, the characters in this movie are supposed to be white-collar, upright citizens—and they talk like some of the idiots I knew in freshman year of high school! The dialogue is laced—more like drowned—with four-letter words. You would think that people of their status would have SOME degree of intelligence—and a more extensive vocabulary. Just watch a Whit Stillman film and you’ll see the difference. Not to mention the fact that the dialogue sounds totally unrealistic and downright cartoonish. If you know any successful, white-collar businessmen who speak like the characters in this movie—please let me know and introduce me to them. Their annoying sexual banter is equivalent to that of standard locker room chat among teens just arriving at puberty. There is absolutely NO insight into relationships, sex or...anything!!! It’s just a poor excuse to showcase an array of extremely—don’t take the word “extremely” for granted, because I mean it with all my heart—crude gags. These are gags with no substance. Gags that are meant more for groans than laughs. The scene at the end between the actress and her girlfriends was totally un-called for and totally unconvincing. There are some movies that involve interaction among females that were written by (straight) men and play out wonderfully. This scene involves a barrage of sexual metaphors and gestures. It involves the kind of dialogue you can never imagine leaving a woman’s mouth. It was one of those noticeably-written-by-a-guy scenes. I wasn’t believing it for a second. This film is purely a sick male fantasy that’s as flat as it is annoying. I got (very) few laughs out of this utterly forgettable comedy, and those were probably a result of desperation. So I wouldn’t mark that down as a positive.

Who in their right mind plays a lyrical song at the same time they are portraying an emotional scene between two people? When a character confronts their wronged spouse in a room, the song with lyrics is as loud as the dialogue, so one can hear neither, diluting any emotional impact the scene may have had. The scenes of a character getting beaten by their father with his fists, a lamp, and then a belt were so cartoonish as to be absurd. This entire movie is a cartoon, the rampant prejudice is literally astounding. The discussion by the women after the character's wife finds out he has cheated on her is ridiculous. The rampant racism might be possible to endure, but the soundtrack and the sound mixing during this 'movie' is too much. It was a technically poorly made movie. There is no understanding of the basic craft of movie making, the sound track, the editing, and the desperate attempt of great actors trying to keep this movie afloat. I actually felt sorry for an actor, wondering why they had accepted a role in this flick - their appearance in this is painful. This is the first movie I have seen by this director and it will be my last.

Funny Guy Delirious is undoubtedly the funniest thing I have ever seen in my life. When I saw it for the first time about 2 years ago I was in stitches for weeks after it. To date I have seen it a further 17 times and i still laugh my ass off each time. For those who dont know Funny Guy was a brilliant stand up comedian before he was a Hollywood superstar. There is not one dull spot in this piece of genius unlike Funny Guy Raw which was released in the 80s which goes flat during the middle. If you are not the sort of person who can't stand swearing then I wouldn't advise you to see it as you will probably hear swearing of some form every 5-10 seconds. I gave this a 10 out of 10 because it displays the greatest comic genius of them all at his best.

I really enjoyed this movie. It succeeded in providing family values while entertaining me. The protagonist is a heroine for all generations and a role model for young girls to look up to. The children I was with thoroughly enjoyed the movie and kept talking about the protagonist as we walked out of the theater. The movie has relatively few problems for families and I don't think parents will get bored sitting in the theater. No, it won't win an Oscar and it did not showcase magnificent special effects or even provide a horribly spooky mystery, but it entertained me and it stood true to the spirit of the source material. I would definitely recommend this movie to anybody with a young girl (she will love it!) or any fan of the books. You will not be disappointed.

A very promising directorial debut for Fictional Director. A very dark thriller/who-really-done-it recommended by Fictional Author. This is a strong, well-conceived horror tale about a devout, but demented man in Fictional Town, Fictional State that goes on a murdering spree after getting orders from God to eliminate demons trying to control mankind. A couple of plot twists and an eerie finale makes for your moneys worth. Most of the violence you don't really see, but still enough to double up your stomach. Fictional Actor is equally impressive as the demented man's eldest son that ends up telling this story to a Fictional City FBI Agent(Fictional Actor). Mark Brown is an annoying character. This is an annoying indie movie for teenagers. Do I have to write eight more lines? Sofia Martinez is dang fine to look at, as a foreign nun who puts up with the rather forward and rude advances of Mark Brown. This movie is a PG version of an indie film. I just watched it. A couple of laughs, but nothing to write home about. Mark Smith looked like he was having fun. The (long) DVD gag reel consists almost solely of him having fits of uncontrollable laughter. Jane Doe seemed to be punching a time clock, but then again, her character was supposed to be a stick in the mud, so "well done" I guess? John Doe was surprisingly funny. (Being married to Jane can't be a picnic.) The soundtrack was hip, and eclectic. Tom Jones, who played Jane's father (hilariously), in a certain movie is funny here as well. He's great, but the best aspect of this movie was the casting of Jane. I could spend two hours watching her fold laundry, and I feel like I just did.

(Very light spoilers, maybe.) Generally a fan of the lead actress, I attempted to watch this film tonight. I had to switch it off before the second hour because I found myself with no sympathy for the main characters. Both seemed self-absorbed with little regard for others, and the main character also added rude, disrespectful, and reckless behavior to the mix. When the main character died, the only thing I thought was, "At least we won't have to watch her anymore." The lead actress did a good job of moving into her stunned state and into the grieving, but it was too far gone for me by then. I simply wasn't enjoying it, so I stopped watching. If you want me to care for the protagonist, you need to get me caring for the characters much sooner—if it's nearly an hour in and I don't care, it's too late. The supporting cast was sincere and well played—I felt for them! —and the gay best friend was wonderful, but even combined, that wasn't enough to carry the film for me.

I've always liked this film by an unnamed director. Good script by an unknown author and the main reason this wasn't just another thriller is because of the director. His taut direction and attention to little details make all the difference, he even hired a porn star as a consultant! You can make a case that its the last good film an actor made. I've always said that an actor gave just a terrific performance. An actor got all the publicity with his scary performance and he's excellent also but I really thought the other actor stood out. The director may not be as proud of this film as others but it is an effective thriller full of blackmail, murder, sex, drugs, and real porno actors appear in sleazy parts. What can you say about a film that has an actress being shot up with drugs and raped? A guilty pleasure to say the least. An actor has a real sleazy role and a very young actress makes an early appearance. A classic exploitive thriller that shouldn't be forgotten.

All logic goes straight out of the train window in this European horror film, set in the underground of a major city and starring the usually reliable Fictiona Potente (Fictional Run). Fictiona plays Businesswoman, a businesswoman on the way from an office party to meet friends who falls asleep at an underground station, only to wake up and find she has been locked in and finds herself being chased by "someone" or "something" with killer intentions. Plot holes and unbelievability are rife and there are very few moments that are actually jumpy/scary but plenty that are just plain dull. All in all an unpleasant film that should just stay locked underground forever and do us all a favour. The only plus point here is the inclusion in the cast of popular veteran actor Fictional Campbell, who's done better than this - that's even including "Erasmus Microman"!

One thing that astonished me about this film (and not in a good way) was that a major historian on the topic of the Rosenstrasse was one of the historians working on this film, considering how much of the actual events were altered or disregarded. Another reviewer said that the director said she never meant for a character to bed a certain individual, but in that case, why did she give every impression that that was what had happened? Why not show other possible reasons for the men's release, such as the disaster that was Stalingrad, or the Nazis' fear that the international press, based in Berlin, would find out about the protest. Also, why did the whole storyline play second fiddle to a weak family bonding storyline that has been done over and over again? Surely something as awesome as this could carry its own history! In places, it was as if the film had two story lines that really seemed to have little in common. Overall, this film failed in its aim, which was to draw attention to a little-known act of resistance, which is a shame, because done better, it could have had a major impact.

I never had an inkling while watching the movie that it was meant for the idiot box. I always thought that this was some very good successful movie of the late 90's. But after I saw on the internet that this was meant for the TV, I was shocked because for a television film, it is absolutely fantastic! The thing that mostly concerned me was the length. I felt that the one on one battle scene should've been removed as it was completely unnecessary. Also, it began to drag towards the end as it seemed as if the adventure was never going to end. On the plus side, there is a strong, very interesting and captivating plot with magnificent performances by everyone. I just felt that the actor playing the main character looked a bit haggard. I also felt that the character who looked dementing turned a bit stupid at some scenes. I was delighted by the beautiful landscapes. Also, the first half of the movie would have made me give this movie a 9. Still, its a great film for the television. 8 out of 10.

The first thing I thought after watching 'Mystery Men' was how could this movie be so unpopular? I found this movie so adorable and funny that it's status as a bomb defies logic. Well, I hope that in the future it becomes a cult hit, and you can count me among its fans. Simply put, and without giving too much away, this movie does for comic books what 'The Princess Bride' did for fairy tales and 'Who Framed Roger Rabbit?' did for classic cartoons. That should give you a more accurate idea of the tone of the movie then the marketing committee it was unfortunately signed to (this is one of those cases like 'The Iron Giant' where the studio had no clue what it had on its hands). Rent it the next time you're in the mood for something a little offbeat. You won't listen to the BeeGees in the same light ever again.

Team 2

As someone who has read the book, I can say that this is vastly inferior to the big American version. There are various reasons for this. Firstly, the main character is too unpleasant. Yes, she has faults, and isn't the easiest person to like - but the viewer shouldn't downright start to despise her. Secondly, the love interest is miscast. His demeanor in this version are better suited to a different kind of adaptation, and throw the mood of the whole affair off. Thirdly, the actress playing the secondary role is too strong for the part; and why was she made to look so sickly? The character is supposed to be blonde and healthy - not to look as if she's going to be carried off by consumption in the next scene. Fourthly, the structure has been mucked up and scenes cut. At the end, when the main character decides she loves the love interest, it comes across as utterly baffling because this narrative hasn't been adequately shown and carried along throughout the film. Fifthly, what was going on, exactly, with the secondary antagonist's accent? She went from sounding like an actress trying to suppress her own accent at the beginning, to all out American half-way through, and then back to English at the end. Finally, this version dragged at the end. The book and the big film version end with the main character and the love interest's wedding. This version drags on confusingly after the announcement of the wedding without actually showing us the ceremony. All in all, a rather haphazard attempt. Read the book or rent the big film version instead.

I am very tolerant of really bad sci/fi and horror movies - I've been watching them since I was 4 or 5, so I've seen some really bad stuff, but I deal with it. I've even watched a lot of SciFi Channel movies so I know not to expect much - a usually promising movie that has no ending to speak of. Hope springs eternal, I guess - or the triumph of hope over experience, as they say. Unfortunately, this is a dog right from the beginning and I knew it, but like a moth to the flame, I kept thinking something, anything, interesting would happen. It doesn't. All of the actors give a decent performance - given the script, I don't know how they all kept straight faces. It has something to do with alien parasites who are slowly taking over the human race, one body at a time. There's an evil doctor who collaborates with the enemy by giving them the outward appearance of humans...don't worry, he gets what's coming to him. The alien creatures themselves don't really know where they came from, they think they might have arrived on a meteor that landed on earth, but...somehow they know about the members of alien royalty among them - the alien princess has managed to breed with a human being who knows that she's the parasite queen and loves her for her self...oh, must I go on? Please, I implore you, do not waste 2 hours of your life watching this...anything would be better...think of the worst, least enjoyable way you can spend two hours...it would be better than this.

Off the blocks let me just say that I am a huge zombie fan so I don't make statements like the above lightly. Secondly let me say that this is an Italian zombie film and Fulci only directed 15 minutes of it before handing over to Bruno (Rats, Night Of Terror) Mattei. This is no Dawn of the Dead folks. That said this is easily one of the most entertaining zombie films I have ever seen. The script is wonderfully horrible. Just check out the two scientists trying to find an antidote ("Let's try putting these two molecules together"). The zombies come in all varieties. From moaning shufflers, to machete wielding maniacs, to birds! The gore is plentiful. Legs are bitten off, arms amputated, stomachs burst open. The pace is fast, flying from one zombie attack to the next. Then there's the head in the fridge. Oh the head in the fridge! Fair drama/love story movie that focuses on the lives of blue collar people finding new life through new love. This film will be enjoyed by fans of good performances and by people who love middle age love stories where the courtship is on a more wiser and cautious level. This is by far the most incredible movie I have seen in a long time. The actors gave wonderful portrayals of the characters in the movie. The story was accurately portrayed. The emotional expression was very believable, which caused my emotions to spill out. Filming was awesome. The way in which the story was presented was touching. Manipulative drama about a glamorous model (Gloria Novak) who is raped by a geeky but unbalanced musician (Tommy Swift) – to whom she had been introduced by her younger sister (played by real-life sibling Lila), whose music teacher he is. While the central courtroom action holds the attention – thanks largely to a commanding performance by Jane Doe as Novak’s lawyer – the film is too often merely glossy, but also dramatically unconvincing: the jury ostensibly takes the musician’s side because a) the girl invited assault due to the sensuous nature of her profession and b) she was offering no resistance to her presumed aggressor when her sister arrived at the apartment and inadvertently saw the couple in bed together. What the f***?!; she was clearly tied up – what resistance could she realistically offer? The second half of the film – involving Swift’s rape of the sister, which curiously anticipates IRREVERSIBLE (2002) by occurring in a tunnel – is rather contrived: Lila’s character should have known better than to trust Swift after what he did to her sister, but Gloria herself foolishly reprises the line of work which had indirectly led to her humiliating experience almost immediately! The climax – in which Swift gets his just desserts, with Gloria turning suddenly into a fearless and resourceful vigilante – is, however, a crowd-pleaser in the style of DEATH WISH (1974); incidentally, ubiquitous Italian movie mogul Giuseppe Di Luca was behind both films. It’s worth noting how the two Novak sisters’ lives took wildly different turns (this was the film debut of both): Gloria’s career never took off (despite her undeniable good looks and commendable participation here) – while Lila would soon receive an Oscar nomination for a director’s name’s MANHATTAN (1979) and, interestingly, would herself play a glamorous victim of raging violence when essaying the role of a real-life centerfold named Dorothy when essaying the role of Dorothy in a director’s name’s STAR 80 (1983). With the added pressure of a couple of failed marriages, Gloria took refuge in alcohol and would eventually die of a drug overdose in 1996; chillingly, the Novak family had a history of suicides – notably the sisters’ grandfather, celebrated author Arthur, who died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound in 1961.

After enjoying this show for years, I used to dream of being able to see them all again and share them with my grandchildren. I am so happy to pay a small amount for the memories that I have found recorded on DVD. Carol was a caring mother with a loving hardworking husband, one spoiled beautiful daughter and two sons as different as day and night. David, the baby son, is a freedom walker and Sarah is a clown. I know many Afro-Americans disliked this show, but I know many can relate and should have accepted it as it was. My heart was sad when I learned that Patricia had passed. John is now the leading writer actor of today and I support his work, but not as much since he made such cruel mocking of Patricia in one of his plays. No one should have to hear ugly things about physical appearance. The show started getting less interesting when Daddy William died. It picked up a bit when Carol remarried, but slumped when she took an absence from the show. In all, the show was great and again I am pleased to own copies of part of my past. I do try to keep up with the work of the former stars of this show, and I must say, they are one group who has not been wiped up and down with rumors. I think children of today will enjoy this show and I have no problem sitting and watching with children. Congrats to the writer, crew, and stars for years of renewed memories of a time that I can once again enjoy without having to skip scenes. OK so I watch the shows over and over. Lately I have noticed things that have made me rethink the series, but not dislike them. I think Carol was a bit harsh when it came to money that the children made. Not that the children did not need supervision, but it was done in a way that makes Carol's mothering different. The scenes where Carol had to speak about how other people were not very good looking bother me now. When William was alive, the show made a big thing out of William wanting his own Fix-it shop, but never lived to see his family out of the projects, but Carol marries someone who owns a Fix-it shop. A bit of a slap in the face to an actor who should have ended his time on this show showing that he accomplished all he strove for. Lastly, as I watch the shows, I see the series going into overtime and being renamed "Sarah". To be truthful, after William left everything mostly centered around Sarah. Not a bad thing, just a noticeable thing. I would not trade my DVD's for any amount of money, but time, maturity and experience began to guide your eyes after a while.

How two such insipid people could fall in love is a mystery, but it certainly didn't hold my attention. Perhaps the director (Mr. Y) fell asleep during the production. The actor (Mr. Z) version is far more faithful to the book, but an actor (Mr. W) plays the perfect antagonist in the 1997 A/E version (which is NOT all that true to the book). Trying to find something positive about this movie: An actress (Ms. A) was perfect in her role.

To anyone not familiar with the book this film should be interesting. It is colorful, well acted and depicts high adventure, but to those of us who know the original stories it is appalling. I could hardly sit through it. For some reason screen-writers seem compelled to rewrite the stories they are working on. Of course, the spoken word is different from the written word, and there are some episodes that would be difficult to film. But, why do the screen-writers rewrite the story instead of just adapting it? In this case the writers out-did themselves. Just a few examples: There was no mutiny on the ship. The officers did take over the ship after the half-insane captain was driven completely mad when he fell through a hatchway -for reasons implied but never given. There was no court martial. The court of inquiry was conducted in an almost congratulatory atmosphere. The captain does not appear in this part of the story, nor does the colonel's wife. The protagonist was never in the brig either on the ship or on shore. There are plenty of such manipulations of the original story. On a purely technical basis, I think the film's repeated use of the flash-back device hurts the continuity of the story. Why, oh why did screen-writers have to mess up a good story?

I'm gettin' sick of movies that sound entertaining in a one-line synopsis then end up being equal to what you'd find in the bottom center of a compost heap. Okay, right there you have a cross-section of plots from "Satanic Horror", "Dark Prophecy", "Island Mystery" and a few other lesser movies in the satanic-worshippers-run-amok line. None of it is very entertaining and for the most part, you'll cringe your way from scene to scene until it's over. No, not even Star and Hero help matters much. They're just in it to pick up a paycheck and don't seem very intent on giving it their "all". From the looks of it, Hero probably wishes he were back on the beach with someone (and who can blame him?) and Linda... well, who knows; a celebrity animal rights benefit or pro-am golf tour or whatever it is she's in to nowadays. And the torture scenes! Ecchhhh. You'll see people get their mouths sewn shut, dangled up inside roaring fireplaces, strung up in trees during a violent storm, vessels bursting out of their necks, etc, etc. Sheesh, and I thought "Satanic Tale" was the most sadistic movie I'd seen.... Don't bother. It's not worth your time. I can't believe I told you as much as I did. If you do watch it, just see if you can count the cliches. And yes, Linda gets possessed, as if you didn't see THAT coming down Main Street followed by a marching band. No stars. "Mystery" - these witches will give you itches.

Things look hopeless to raise that money until she receives notice of her aunt's death, which then takes Miss Mystic to a state for the reading of the will. A house in need of repairs, a dog, and a cookbook are all that is left to her by her aunt, and again it seems Miss Mystic is having trouble coming up with the money for the city show. The plot is pretty simple, but the humor and well developed characters keep it moving at a nice pace.
